sources.entry: Jackett | Torrent indexer API proxy for the *arr stack

summary.one_liner: Jackett is a self-hosted proxy server that translates requests from apps like Sonarr and Radarr into tracker-specific queries for torrent and usenet indexers, returning results in Torznab or TorrentPotato format.
summary.what_it_does: Jackett runs as a local web server that acts as a bridge between media apps and torrent trackers. It translates incoming search queries into site-specific HTTP requests, parses the HTML or JSON responses, and returns results in a standardized Torznab or TorrentPotato format. The README lists a very large set of public, semi-private and private trackers it supports, with some marked as lacking an active maintainer. It offers an internal search cache with configurable TTL and result limits, and an optional FlareSolverr integration for Cloudflare-protected indexers. It also provides filter and aggregate "all" indexer endpoints that combine results across configured indexers, and a set of command-line switches for port, data folder, and update behavior.
use_cases: Feed torrent search results to Sonarr or Radarr
Search many private and public trackers from one API
Set up a Torznab indexer for a download client
Run an indexer proxy on a home server or Raspberry Pi
Bypass Cloudflare protection on indexers with FlareSolverr
Combine results from several indexers into one feed
how_to_run: Linux: cd /opt && sudo tar -xz (extract the release), then cd /opt/Jackett && sudo ./install_service_systemd.sh
Run without installing as a service: extract the release and run ./jackett
Docker: see the LinuxServer.io Jackett Docker image (README points to external instructions)
macOS: double-click install_service_macos from the extracted release
notable: Supports public, semi-private and private trackers, with a long list of named indexers
Torznab and TorrentPotato API compatibility for *arr apps
Filter indexer endpoint lets you query subsets by type, tag, language, or health status
Optional FlareSolverr integration for Cloudflare-protected trackers
Web UI on default port 9117 with Windows, Linux, macOS and Docker installs
caveats: Trackers marked as invite-needed have no active maintainer and may be broken
Only versions 0.24.x and later are supported, with Windows 10 1607+ and macOS 13.0+ required
Heavy use can get you banned by tracker sites; the README warns about request volume
ARMv6 and older systems require Mono, which the README notes can be unstable
